newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Gov't may outlaw Colombian truckers' strike.
newsitem.headline: Gov't may outlaw Colombian truckers' strike.

text.p: BOGOTA, April 17 Reuter - Transportation Minister Carlos Hernan Lopez said the Colombian government may move to outlaw a strike by truck drivers set to begin at midnight Saturday.
"The strike has all the characteristics of being declared illegal because the government has already complied with 85 percent of the drivers' demands," Lopez told a news conference.

He did not elaborate, but said "military measures of a preventive type" would be used "to guarantee the transportation of cargo and passengers" if the work stoppage by the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association ACC goes forward as planned.
Lopez said talks with ACC leaders had been set for Friday, however, and held out hope that a negotiated settlement could be reached before the weekend strike deadline.
In his remarks, Lopez also raised fears that leftist guerrillas would somehow seek to take advantage of the strike and add to Colombia's pressing law-and-order problems.
"I'm afraid that subversives may try to take advantage of it and that there are interests at play that have nothing to do with transportation," he said.

The ACC, which represents about 80 percent of Colombia's truckers, set the April 20 strike deadline in March to protest what its leaders describe as the failure, by the government and private transportation companies, to fulfill terms of an agreement ending a crippling 11-day strike last October.
That strike paralyzed virtually all of the country's highway freight, including about 200,000 60-kg bags of coffee.
